attributions.surface_quote: they will become sublime through the remainder of the Light

canonical_statement: The physical body acts as a barrier to the full realization of spiritual truth.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: no one who wears the body will be able to complete these things

canonical_statement: Spiritual liberation is achieved through the separation of thought from the physical vessel.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: when his thought separates from the body, then these things may be revealed

canonical_statement: Humanity is divided into two ontological categories: those possessing the light of the Spirit and those belonging to the Darkness of Nature.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: those who possess the particle of the mind... for they are seed of the universal Darkness

canonical_statement: Entities lacking the Spirit and Faith are subject to dissolution within the Darkness.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: those who do not share in the Spirit of light and in Faith will dissolve

canonical_statement: The physical world and its elemental forces are hostile to the manifestation of the Spirit.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: The winds and the demons will hate them. And the bondage of the body is severe.

canonical_statement: The material world and its forms are subject to a cyclical temporal dissolution.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: two times in the day of the water and the forms of Nature

canonical_statement: The righteous soul is extracted from the material realm through the intervention of Faith.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Faith disturbs them in order to take to herself the righteous one

canonical_statement: Individual thought or consciousness requires activation or invocation by the divine Word.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: it is necessary that the thought be called by the Word

canonical_statement: The material world, symbolized by water, is a state of bondage and limitation for the Spirit.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: from the water to the water there is bondage

canonical_statement: Ritual baptism in water is ineffective for spiritual purification and perpetuates ignorance.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: they are deceived by manifold demons, thinking that through baptism... he will take away sins

canonical_statement: The unbegotten Spirit exists outside the domain of material nature and its associated limitations.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: only in the unbegotten Spirit... has the water not been mentioned

canonical_statement: Individual identity is composed of layered garments or manifestations acquired through cosmic descent.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: all my garments which I put on in all the clouds

canonical_statement: At the end of time, the soul's manifestations return to their origin in the unbegotten Spirit.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: in the last day they will rest in their root, i.e. in the unbegotten Spirit

canonical_statement: The material world is characterized by inherent wickedness and chaos that seeks to entrap divine consciousness.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: the wickedness of Nature might be ended. For she wished at that time to snare me.

canonical_statement: The process of salvation involves the separation of light from darkness.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: the light was about to separate from the Darkness

canonical_statement: Perception and spiritual vision are the primary mechanisms for transcending the material order.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Blessed is the eye which has seen thee, and the mind which has supported thy majesty

canonical_statement: The material realm functions through a cycle of error and vain effort that must be terminated by divine intervention.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: she will cease from every vain effort of Nature and chaos.

canonical_statement: The human consciousness must detach from bodily identification to perceive divine truth.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Do not let your thought have dealings with the body.

canonical_statement: Divine communication adapts its form and language to the specific nature of the recipient.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: I spoke according to the language of each one.

canonical_statement: Faith acts as a metaphysical force capable of governing and overturning the natural order.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Nature was handed over to Faith, that she might overturn her.

canonical_statement: The material world is characterized by a restless, cyclical motion originating from darkness.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Nature brought forth a turning motion while wandering night and day.

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness can transcend the darkness of the material realm through the reception of divine light.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: I came forth from the Darkness and I walked in Faith.

canonical_statement: The material world is a burdened, chaotic state that obscures the true nature of the mind.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Nature is burdened, and she is troubled.

canonical_statement: Access to the underlying reality of existence is restricted to the mind that possesses the original likeness.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: None will be able to open the forms of the Womb except the mind alone.

canonical_statement: Liberation from the material condition requires the shedding of darkness and the adoption of the light of the mind.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: They will strip off the burden of Darkness; they will put on the Word.

canonical_statement: The material world is governed by chaotic, non-divine entities that induce error and disorder.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Demons who have a name which is senseless... govern the world with their teaching.

canonical_statement: The current era of material existence is finite and destined for destruction.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: The era of Nature is approaching destruction.

canonical_statement: The material world is subject to the governance of a specific entity or force.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: He will reign over the world from the east to the west.

canonical_statement: The material world and its forms are temporary and destined for dissolution into a primordial state.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: the forms of Nature will be destroyed... just as they were from the beginning.

canonical_statement: The human mind or spirit is distinct from the physical body and can separate from it upon death.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: my mind began to separate from the body of darkness.

canonical_statement: The physical body acts as a burden or a state of sleep from which the consciousness awakens.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: I arose as it were from the burden of my body, I awoke as if from a long sleep.

canonical_statement: True spiritual liberation involves knowing the source or power in which one's thought rests during the state of embodiment.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Blessed are they who knew, when they slept, in what power their thought rested.

canonical_statement: The Spirit possesses a distinct, non-material essence separate from the works of Nature.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: For where the power of the Spirit has gone there are my sweet waters.

canonical_statement: The material world is a temporary, burdensome state that obscures the true nature of the spirit.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Nature has burdened them for a short time.

canonical_statement: The soul's liberation involves the separation of thought from the darkness of the material world upon the consummation of time.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: When the consummation has come... their thoughts will separate from the Darkness.

canonical_statement: The ultimate state of the liberated spirit is an ineffable, formless light.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: They will be in the ineffable light of the unbegotten Spirit without a form.

canonical_statement: Time is a construct that can be compressed or accelerated through the movement of the righteous.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: The righteous one visits during twelve periods that he may visit them during one period.

canonical_statement: The material world is characterized by error and death, from which the soul must guard itself.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Blessed are they who guard themselves against the heritage of death.

canonical_statement: Salvation is achieved through the acquisition of esoteric knowledge.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: knowledge is the means of salvation.

canonical_statement: The creator deity of the material world is malevolent and ignorant.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: The God of this world is evil and ignorant.

canonical_statement: The physical body and worldly powers are illusory or counterfeit.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: all his minions are mere counterfeits and laughingstocks.

canonical_statement: The historical crucifixion of the Savior was a docetic event rather than a physical reality.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Simon of Cyrene is crucified in the place of the laughing Jesus.

canonical_statement: Individual souls share a fundamental, eternal brotherhood and unity.

attributions.chapter: THE PARAPHRASE OF SHEM ( V I I ,7 )
attributions.surface_quote: Rest then with me, my fellow spirits and my brothers, for ever.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is a state of rest within an ineffable, perfect light.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: the perfect Majesty is at rest in the ineffable light

canonical_statement: The individual consciousness and the divine source exist in a state of mutual indwelling.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: It is I who am in you and you are in me

canonical_statement: The multiplicity of spirits originates from a single, unified source.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: they all had a single mind, since it is out of one

canonical_statement: The material world was structured by a lower, independent creative will.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: those who were in the world had been prepared by the will of Sophia

canonical_statement: Physical bodies are constructed from lower elemental matter by Sophia.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: elements below to build bodily dwellings from them

canonical_statement: Material existence is inherently transient and subject to destruction.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: they ended in destruction in the dwellings in which they were

canonical_statement: The divine Monad provides a life-giving word that transcends material structures.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: receive the life-giving word of the ineffable Monad

canonical_statement: The consciousness of the Son of Light can inhabit and displace existing occupants of physical bodies.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I visited a bodily dwelling. I cast out the one who was in it

canonical_statement: The true divine identity is transcendent and originates from above the heavens, distinct from the earthly, material form.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I am from above the heavens; I am a stranger to the regions below.

canonical_statement: The material world and its archontic rulers are characterized by ignorance and a false sense of sovereignty.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I laughed joyfully when I examined his empty glory.

canonical_statement: The physical body and the material realm are constructs designed to obscure the true nature of the Man of Truth.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: They reveal the realm of the angels, which humanity was seeking in order that they may not know the Man of Truth.

canonical_statement: The divine essence is not subject to death; the appearance of death is a mechanism to maintain the structure of the lower archontic hierarchy.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I did not really die lest their archangel become empty.

canonical_statement: The archontic perception of reality is limited and distorted by their own lack of divine insight.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: They are small and senseless in their empty Ennoia.

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine source exists in a state of primordial stillness.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: The whole greatness of the Fatherhood of the Spirit was at rest.

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness or emanation originates from eternal, incomprehensible divine principles.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I have an Ennoia of a single emanation from the eternal ones.

canonical_statement: The introduction of higher consciousness into the material realm disrupts established angelic and archontic hierarchies.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I placed the small Ennoia in the world, having disturbed them.

canonical_statement: Material reality and its governing structures are subject to decay and eventual dissolution.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: The Seraphim and Cherubim, since their glory will fade.

canonical_statement: The physical death of a divine being is an illusion perceived only by those in a state of ignorance.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I did not die in reality but in appearance.

canonical_statement: The true self is capable of altering its form and appearance to move through lower realms undetected.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: I was altering my shapes, changing from form to form.

canonical_statement: The material world and its archontic powers are characterized by error, blindness, and empty glory.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: The wealth of the archons and the offspring of their error, of their empty glory.

canonical_statement: Divine action in the lower realms is governed by the will of the Father above.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: Accomplish what I desired by the will of the Father above.

canonical_statement: There exists a transcendent, hidden realm of existence that is imperishable and beyond human perception.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: The height where I was in all these aeons, which no one has seen nor known.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is an undivided, permanent, and ineffable mystery.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: an undefiled mystery... undivided, universal, and permanent.

canonical_statement: The soul originates from a higher realm and achieves liberation by returning to the Father.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: the soul, the one from the height... standing before the Father.

canonical_statement: Liberated souls achieve a state of mutual recognition and union with the divine.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: Since they see me, they are being seen and are mixed with them.

canonical_statement: The material world and its authorities are characterized by ignorance and limitation.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: fled from the fire of the seven Authorities... zealous service of ignorance.

canonical_statement: Human liberation involves the shedding of the old self and the adoption of a new, enlightened identity.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: having shed zealous service of ignorance... having put on the new man.

canonical_statement: The individual consciousness is ontologically identical to the Father.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: the will of the Father, who is I.

canonical_statement: The descent of consciousness into material bodies is a departure from a primordial home.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: After we went forth from our home, and came down to this world

canonical_statement: The material world is characterized by the presence of hostile entities known as archons.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: we took counsel about the destruction of the archons.

canonical_statement: Ignorance of one's true identity and origin results in a state of spiritual servitude.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: not knowing who they are... they served two masters

canonical_statement: The enlightened possess a mind derived from the Father, existing in an ineffable mystery.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: we have a mind of the Father in an ineffable mystery

canonical_statement: Material existence and worldly doctrines are imitations of a higher, undefiled truth.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: archons do not know that it is an ineffable union... of which they made an imitation

canonical_statement: True spiritual authority is characterized by the absence of desire and the possession of an internal law.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )
attributions.surface_quote: They do not desire because they have authority, and a law from themselves

canonical_statement: The divine essence is united with the individual will, operating without external constraint or force.

attributions.chapter: THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE GREAT SETH ( V I I ,2 )

canonical_statement: Cognition of the divine requires the reception of an external, transcendent light to overcome the darkness of the mind.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He who is in darkness will not be able to see anything unless he receives the light.

canonical_statement: The individual mind must orient itself toward higher, non-terrestrial realities to achieve understanding.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Do not allow your mind to stare downward, but rather let it look by means of the light at things above.

canonical_statement: The soul is capable of existing in a state of profound ignorance regarding its true nature and guide.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: O soul, persistent one, in what ignorance you exist!

canonical_statement: The Underworld functions as a literal or metaphysical place of perdition and entrapment for the soul.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The Underworld is open wide for the soul.

canonical_statement: Divine beings can assume human likenesses to interact with and redeem human souls.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: How many likenesses did Christ take on because of you?

canonical_statement: The soul's state of existence is determined by its moral orientation and fundamental choices.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The fundamental choice, which is humility of heart, is the gift of Christ.

canonical_statement: Moral degradation and attachment to base desires result in the loss of human reason and the acquisition of an animal-like existence.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: A soul which has been found in death will be without reason.

canonical_statement: The soul possesses the capacity to release itself from metaphysical bonds through the rejection of desire.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Release yourself from every bond so that you may acquire freedom.

canonical_statement: The human mind functions as a mirror reflecting the divine intellect.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The mind is a mirror of the divine.

canonical_statement: True wisdom is attained through the internal recognition of one's origin in the transcendent.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Know yourself to know the Father.

canonical_statement: The material world is a transient state distinct from the eternal nature of the soul.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The world is passing; the soul is eternal.

canonical_statement: The human soul functions as a vessel that can transition between being a temple of divinity or a tomb of dead, animalistic impulses.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: You were a temple, but you have made yourself a tomb.

canonical_statement: The individual possesses an internal light that must be actively maintained to prevent spiritual death.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Light the light within you. Do not extinguish it.

canonical_statement: The Christ figure is ontologically identical to Wisdom, the Word, and the source of life.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The Tree of Life is Christ. He is Wisdom.

canonical_statement: Self-knowledge and introspection are the primary methods for accessing hidden spiritual treasures and avoiding error.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Knock on yourself as upon a door.

canonical_statement: Reason is the essential faculty that distinguishes the human soul from animalistic existence.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Entrust yourself to reason and remove yourself from animalism.

canonical_statement: Spiritual transformation involves the death of the old self to receive life from the divine.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS (V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Raise your dead who have died... They shall live again.

canonical_statement: The human capacity for reason allows for the mastery of base impulses and external negative influences.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: It is possible for you through reasoning to conquer them.

canonical_statement: The human soul possesses the potential to achieve ontological likeness to the Divine through virtuous conduct.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Although he is a man who exists on earth, he makes himself like God.

canonical_statement: The human body and consciousness serve as an internal temple for the indwelling of the Divine.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Let him dwell in the temple which is within you.

canonical_statement: The presence of the Divine within the individual acts as a protective barrier against external spiritual or moral corruption.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Whenever the enemies do not see Christ in you, then they will come into you.

canonical_statement: Separation from the Divine principle results in the vulnerability of the soul to destructive external forces.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Every man who is separated from him falls into the claws of the wild beasts.

canonical_statement: The ultimate purpose of the divine incarnation is to facilitate the ontological transformation of humanity into a state of likeness to God.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He became like God... that man might become like God.

canonical_statement: Human intellectual capacity is inherently limited and insufficient for comprehending the nature of the Divine or the structure of the heavens.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Who will be able to comprehend the Divinity or the divinities of the heavens?

canonical_statement: The material world is subject to a process of renewal intended to eliminate imperfection and manifest the brilliance of the Father.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The Life of Heaven wishes to renew all, that he may cast out that which is weak.

canonical_statement: Divine power operates through the subversion of worldly hierarchies, specifically exalting humility over strength and pride.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He put to shame haughtiness through humility; he who has cast down the strong.

canonical_statement: The Logos functions as the intermediary emanation of the Divine, acting as the mirror and image of the Father's nature.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He is the spotless mirror of the working of God, and he is the image.

canonical_statement: The Logos serves as the vitalizing principle that sustains and governs all living things, analogous to the soul's relationship to the body.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Just as the soul gives life to all the members, he rules all with power.

canonical_statement: Human existence is defined by a spiritual struggle against opposing cosmic powers, requiring constant vigilance and moral effort.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Fight the great fight as long as the fight lasts, while all the powers are staring.

canonical_statement: The Divine consciousness experiences emotional resonance with the states of individual souls, mourning their failures and rejoicing in their purity.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He is troubled on behalf of everyone, and he rejoices and also mourns.

canonical_statement: Individual identity is subject to transformation, requiring the abandonment of the 'old man' to achieve spiritual elevation.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Raise yourself up when you have left your old man behind like an eagle.

canonical_statement: The creative agency of the Father is mediated through the Son, who acts as the formative principle of all existence.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The hand of the Father is Christ, and it forms all.

canonical_statement: The Divine exists in a state of omnipresence that transcends spatial location, being simultaneously everywhere and nowhere.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He dwells in every place, and also he is in no place.

canonical_statement: Divine omniscience encompasses all temporal states, rendering the concept of testing or discovery by the Creator logically impossible.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: God does not need to put any man to the test; he knows all things.

canonical_statement: The nature of the Divine is characterized by a paradoxical duality of being simultaneously fully revealed and fundamentally incomprehensible.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: He is revealed to everyone, and yet he is very hidden.

canonical_statement: All created entities exist within the Divine, functioning as manifestations of the Word, which serves as the image of the Father.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: All dwell in God, things which have come into being through the Word.

canonical_statement: Self-knowledge is the necessary prerequisite for the knowledge of all spiritual hierarchies and divine entities.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: If you do not know yourself, you will not be able to know all of these.

canonical_statement: The individual consciousness contains an internal gateway to the divine, accessible through self-directed inquiry.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Open the door for yourself that you may know the One who is.

canonical_statement: The material world is governed by hostile powers that must be transcended through spiritual alignment.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Prepare yourself to escape from the world-rulers of darkness.

canonical_statement: The purification of the external life is a functional requirement for the purification of the internal consciousness.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Purify yourself toward the outward life in order that you may purify the inward.

canonical_statement: Humanity possesses a lineage of divine knowledge transmitted through specific ancestral figures.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Sethian gnosis had been revealed anew in the latter days.

canonical_statement: The human form is a derivative likeness of the divine, transmitted through successive generations.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Seth is a son in the likeness of his father Adam, as Adam is in the likeness of God.

canonical_statement: The structure of the divine is inherently threefold.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: The expansion from the original two steles... represents the influence of Neoplatonic conceptions of the divine triad.

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine reality is structured as a triad consisting of the Father, the Mother, and the Son.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: god: the Selfbegotten Son, the male virgin Barbelo (mother), and the Unbegotten Father.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness can achieve a state of total perfection through mystical union with divine aeons.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: I joined with them all... I became all-perfect.

canonical_statement: The structure of reality includes transcendent realms or aeons accessible through visionary ascent.

attributions.chapter: THE TEACHINGS OF SILVANUS ( V I I ,4 )
attributions.surface_quote: Ecstatic trips through the heavens are well attested.

canonical_statement: The ultimate nature of the divine is structured as a triad of Existence, Life, and Mind.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Neoplatonic philosophical terminology abounds in the text, especially the Existence-Life-Mind triad in the deity.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness can achieve a progressive ascent through distinct stages to reach the divine nature.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: The three subdivisions of the text thus correspond to the three stages or levels in the worshippers’ ascent.

canonical_statement: The process of spiritual ascent is cyclical, requiring a return from higher states of consciousness to lower ones.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: One must return from the third back down to the second and first.

canonical_statement: The relationship between the divine source and the individual consciousness is one of non-biological generation.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: I, as thine own Son, Emmacha Seth, whom thou didst beget without begetting

canonical_statement: The individual consciousness is fundamentally identical to the divine mind.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: thou art my mind

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine principle is unbegotten and exists as the source of all being.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Thou art unbegotten... Thou art he who is.

canonical_statement: The divine essence is transcendent, existing as a race apart from the perceptible world.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Thou art from another race, for thou art not similar.

canonical_statement: The divine unity remains singular even while manifesting as a multiplicity throughout the universe.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Thou didst continue being one... Thou wast divided everywhere.

canonical_statement: Individual perfection is achieved through union with the divine source.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: We bless thee... as the perfect individuals, perfect on account of thee.

canonical_statement: The perceptible world derives its existence and knowledge of reality from the divine source.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: The perceptible world too knows thee because of thee.

canonical_statement: The ultimate source of reality is a non-being that transcends existence.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: the one who truly pre-exists because he is a non-being

canonical_statement: The divine monad manifests as a triple power while remaining essentially one.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: thou a triple power, thou a great monad from a pure monad

canonical_statement: Multiplicity and individual forms arise through the division of the singular divine essence.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: begetter of multiplicity according to a division of all who really are

canonical_statement: Manifest reality is derived from the shadow of the transcendent Father.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: thou art from a shadow of him

canonical_statement: The divine essence empowers and sustains all dualities and differences within existence.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: thou hast empowered him who is equal and him who is not equal

canonical_statement: The ultimate source of existence is a non-being that precedes all manifested beings and existences.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: non-being, existence which is before existences, first being which is before beings

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness is a derivative reflection or shadow of a higher, pre-existent divine reality.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: we are each a shadow of thee as thou art a shadow of that first pre-existent one

canonical_statement: Salvation is achieved through the acquisition of direct knowledge of the ultimate divine source.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Knowledge of thee, it is the salvation of us all.

canonical_statement: The divine source is the singular origin and sustainer of life, mind, and truth.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: On account of thee is life; from thee is life. On account of thee is mind.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is a singular, living spirit that exists beyond the capacity of linguistic expression.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Thou art an only and living spirit. We are not able to express him.

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine principle is a singular, unified existence that constitutes the life, mind, and essence of all beings.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Thou art the existence of them all. Thou art the life of them all.

canonical_statement: The divine principle is self-begotten and exists prior to its own manifestation.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Thou who existeth within thyself, thou who art before thyself.

canonical_statement: The process of spiritual ascent through cosmic levels is identical in structure to the process of descent.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: The way of ascent is the way of descent.

canonical_statement: Perfection and impassability are attained through the remembrance and glorification of the divine source.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: He who will remember these and give glory always will become perfect.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is beyond the capacity of language and naming.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: How shall we give thee a name? We do not have it.

canonical_statement: The source of spiritual authority and lineage is identified as a paternal principle.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: This book belongs to the fatherhood.

canonical_statement: The manifestation or expression of the divine principle is identified as the son.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: It is the son who wrote it.

canonical_statement: The physical world is an emanation from a singular, transcendent, and invisible divine source.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: a high god named the thrice powerful Invisible Spirit from whom everything else has emanated.

canonical_statement: The material realm represents the lowest and most ignorant state of existence.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: The physical earth and its inhabitants represent the lowest and most ignorant level.

canonical_statement: The consciousness of the divine source manifests as an intermediate system of aeons.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: a vast aeon system called Barbelo and understood as the “thought” of the Spirit.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness can transcend the physical body to access higher realms of knowledge.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: Leaving his physical body behind on earth, he ascended with the angel.

canonical_statement: The changeable material world originates from an unchanging, eternal source.

attributions.chapter: THE THREE STELES OF SETH ( V I I ,5 )
attributions.surface_quote: how this changeable world came into existence from an unchanging source.

canonical_statement: The universe is structured in hierarchical layers, where each level is derived from and less perfect than the one preceding it.

attributions.surface_quote: each successive layer of the universe is formed on the basis of the models above

canonical_statement: The fundamental triad of existence, mind, and life constitutes the primary aeonic structure of reality.

attributions.surface_quote: identification of the three Barbelo aeons with the philosophical triad of existence, mind, and life

canonical_statement: The human condition involves an inherent separation from somatic, psychic, and desire-based states of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: I parted from the somatic darkness in me and the psychic chaos

canonical_statement: The perceptible world and its creator are distinct from the true, infinite nature of the All.

attributions.surface_quote: I reproved the dead creation within me and the divine Cosmocrater

canonical_statement: The soul originates from a holy, transcendent source despite being temporarily mixed with material existence.

attributions.surface_quote: I came into being through a holy, yet mixed

canonical_statement: It is possible for the individual consciousness to attain a spiritual state that transcends the divine creator of the perceptible world.

attributions.surface_quote: grow strong in a holy spirit higher than god

canonical_statement: The ultimate source of reality is an invisible, undivided, and self-begotten spirit that precedes all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: those who exist... come from an invisible, undivided and self-begotten spirit

canonical_statement: Existence is a mixture of divine powers, essences, and material forms, yet originates from a source beyond existence.

attributions.surface_quote: existence is mixed... with the god of the unborn Kalyptos

canonical_statement: The human spirit possesses an origin that is distinct from and prior to its incarnation in the perceptible world.

attributions.surface_quote: I did not cease seeking a resting place worthy of my spirit

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the eternal realms provides salvation and liberation from the cycle of death and ignorance.

attributions.surface_quote: why have you gone mad as if you were ignorant of the great eternals

canonical_statement: The soul's origin and lineage are rooted in divine or angelic hierarchies.

attributions.surface_quote: you are the father of your race or that Iolaos is your father

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness undergoes cyclical returns to the material world for the purpose of spiritual instruction.

attributions.surface_quote: You will return to them another time to preach to a living race

canonical_statement: The material world is characterized by a brief duration relative to the eternal struggle of the aeons.

attributions.surface_quote: the struggle of the aeon is great but one’s time in this world is short

canonical_statement: The human soul can transcend the material world and the thirteen aeons to reach higher realms of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: I was rescued from the whole world and the thirteen aeons in it.

canonical_statement: Spiritual purification through ritual baptism is necessary to ascend through successive aeons.

attributions.surface_quote: washing there seven times in living water, once for each of the aeons.

canonical_statement: The true self is a power that exists independently of and superior to material darkness.

attributions.surface_quote: I knew that the power in me was set over the darkness.

canonical_statement: Higher reality is structured as a hierarchy of aeons and emanations originating from a self-begotten root.

attributions.surface_quote: I stood there after having seen light from the truth which really exists, from its self-begotten root.

canonical_statement: Individual identity can be transformed into a divine state through the reception of celestial images and sealing.

attributions.surface_quote: I received the image of the glories there. I became like one of them.

canonical_statement: The soul undergoes progressive stages of purification and ontological elevation through repeated ritual baptism.

attributions.surface_quote: I was baptized for the second time... I became an angel of the male race.

canonical_statement: The structure of the aeons is non-linear or recursive, where higher states of being correspond to inverted numerical positions.

attributions.surface_quote: I stood upon the second aeon which is the third.

canonical_statement: Identity is fluid and capable of ascending through distinct hierarchical categories of angelic existence.

attributions.surface_quote: I became an angel... I became a holy angel... I became a perfect angel.

canonical_statement: The material world is a derivative construct generated through a series of reflections of the divine.

attributions.surface_quote: With a reflection of a reflection he worked at producing the world.

canonical_statement: The physical world is governed by a ruler who is an origin of matter and darkness.

attributions.surface_quote: He condemned its ruler to death because he was an origin of matter.

canonical_statement: Individual human differences are rooted in the diversity of souls and their varying origins.

attributions.surface_quote: Are there souls different from souls? Why are people different from one another?

canonical_statement: The material realm is a perishable model that paradoxically reveals eternal indestructibility.

attributions.surface_quote: The airy-earth reveals the perishable ones by its indestructibility.

canonical_statement: The creation of the world resulted from a flawed perception or misapprehension of the divine by a lower power.

attributions.surface_quote: He saw a reflection. In relation to the reflection which he saw, he created the world.

canonical_statement: The aeons exist as eternal, immutable realities that serve as the archetypal source for copies within the lower world.

attributions.surface_quote: It is in the following way that the copies of the aeons exist.

canonical_statement: Individual souls are positioned within the hierarchy of existence based on their internal power and degree of illumination.

attributions.surface_quote: Souls are located according to the power they have in themselves.

canonical_statement: The process of spiritual progression involves transitioning from the copies of reality to the true, original forms of those realities.

attributions.surface_quote: They are removed one by one from the copy of Exile to the Exile that really exists.

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the divine structure is inherent to the soul, rendering external inquiry into these matters redundant for the enlightened.

attributions.surface_quote: Why are you calling on me and asking about those things which you know?

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality is composed of three fundamental principles: Existence, Blessedness, and Life.

attributions.surface_quote: These (three) are Existence, Blessedness and Life.

canonical_statement: The three fundamental principles originate from a singular source, the Barbelo aeon.

attributions.surface_quote: origins are three because they have appeared in a single origin of the Barbelo aeon.

canonical_statement: The fundamental principles of reality derive from a source that transcends their own nature.

attributions.surface_quote: they appeared from that which is far better than themselves.

canonical_statement: The Invisible Spirit serves as the ultimate source or fountainhead from which all divine powers and entities originate.

attributions.surface_quote: the Invisible Spirit is a fountain of them all.

canonical_statement: Divine entities and aeons are structured through specific, distinct 'waters' or baptismal states corresponding to Vitality, Blessedness, and Existence.

attributions.surface_quote: It is the water of life that belongs to Vitality... water of Blessedness... water of Existence.

canonical_statement: Self-limitation is a fundamental mechanism by which a divine being establishes its true existence.

attributions.surface_quote: It is he because he limits himself.

canonical_statement: The material world is structured and bounded by divine intervention to prevent it from remaining endless and formless.

attributions.surface_quote: In order that this world might not be endless and formless, he placed a [ . . . ] over it.

canonical_statement: Self-knowledge is a prerequisite for a soul to realize its own nature and attain a state of perfect, limitless life.

attributions.surface_quote: he who knows himself [ . . . ] become [limitless . . . ]

canonical_statement: The self-begotten aeons are organized into four perfect entities, each possessing a distinct form and corresponding divine water.

attributions.surface_quote: the self-begotten aeons are four perfect entities.

canonical_statement: The Autogenes functions as the primary governing entity for its constituent aeons and angelic emanations.

attributions.surface_quote: The Autogenes is the chief archon of his own aeons and angels as his parts.

canonical_statement: Higher metaphysical entities exist in a state of non-locality, being present everywhere without being contained by any specific place.

attributions.surface_quote: They are in every place that he loves and desires, yet they are not in any place.

canonical_statement: The nature of divine beings is incorporeal, yet they possess a mode of existence that transcends the category of incorporeality.

attributions.surface_quote: They have capacity for spirit, for they are incorporeal yet are better than incorporeal.

canonical_statement: The Kalyptos serves as the ontological origin and causal forefather of the Autogenes and subsequent divine emanations.

attributions.surface_quote: The self-begotten Kalyptos pre-exists because he is an origin of the Autogenes.

canonical_statement: Individual identity is achieved through the cognitive unification of the self with the totality of divine emanations.

attributions.surface_quote: If one joins oneself with all these, one is that water which belongs to Kalyptos.

canonical_statement: Reality originates from a single source and undergoes a process of division and subsequent reintegration.

attributions.surface_quote: how they all appear from a single origin, how all who are joined come to be divided

canonical_statement: The soul possesses distinct faculties—soul, mind, and spirit—each capable of perceiving specific levels of divine reality.

attributions.surface_quote: He can see with his perfect soul those who belong to Autogenes; with his mind, those who belong to the Triple Male

canonical_statement: Spiritual purification is achieved through successive stages of knowledge and ritual 'washings' corresponding to different aeonic levels.

attributions.surface_quote: one understands these things, one has washed in the washing of Kalyptos.

canonical_statement: The ultimate state of being involves stripping away worldly attachments and knowledge to attain a state of pure, unconditioned existence.

attributions.surface_quote: if he strips off the world and lays aside knowledge, then because he follows the ways of the others

canonical_statement: The divine reality is self-contained, with no part of the individual existing outside of the divine totality.

attributions.surface_quote: There is nothing of his outside of him.

attributions.surface_quote: salvation was the free expression of his own visionary imagination.

canonical_statement: The material universe is a restrictive, artificial construct designed to limit and contain spiritual essence.

attributions.surface_quote: The heavens squared by a line... spirits mournd their bondage

canonical_statement: The creator of the material realm is a false deity who falsely claims absolute divinity and equality with the supreme source.

attributions.surface_quote: Am I not God. Who is Equal to me.

canonical_statement: Individual souls are trapped, harvested, or dispersed by the demiurgic power into the material structure.

attributions.surface_quote: his skirt filld with immortal souls... fly the souls from Urizen’s strong hand

canonical_statement: The creator of the material universe is distinct from the true God and is inherently malevolent.

attributions.surface_quote: He separates the true God from nature, and regards the creator as evil.

canonical_statement: The material universe is a deceptive mask or facade concealing a fundamental reality of death.

attributions.surface_quote: The material universe is but a mask, a cosmetic behind which lies death.

canonical_statement: Matter possesses an inherent, persistent, and brutal quality that resists spiritual abatement.

attributions.surface_quote: Matter in end will never abate / His ancient brutal claim.

canonical_statement: The creator of the material world may be ignorant of the higher divine source.

attributions.surface_quote: Ahab flings an accusation at the creator that conjures Yaldabaoth’s ignorance.

canonical_statement: The individual consciousness is ignorant of its own origin and ontological status.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou knowest not how came ye, hence callest thyself unbegotten.

canonical_statement: There exists a transcendent reality or entity that encompasses and surpasses the creator of the current temporal order.

attributions.surface_quote: There is some unsuffusing thing beyond thee, to whom all thy eternity is but time.

canonical_statement: The human condition is characterized by a fall from original unity into a state of division.

attributions.surface_quote: The fall into Division, and Resurrection to Unity.

canonical_statement: The human psyche is composed of distinct, conflicting elements, specifically the pneuma and the psyche.

attributions.surface_quote: The two speakers are precisely the pneuma and the psyche of Gnostic formulation.

canonical_statement: Human imagination functions as a mechanism for transcending the material world and the cycle of reincarnation.

attributions.surface_quote: If but imagination scorn the earth... Deliver from the crime of death and birth.

canonical_statement: The human soul is fundamentally distinct from the physical body and seeks liberation from biological existence.

attributions.surface_quote: Fastened to a dying animal... Once out of nature I shall never take my form.

canonical_statement: History is governed by cyclical shifts in the world spirit that dictate the transition between religious epochs.

attributions.surface_quote: The turning of the ages was recorded... envisioning the approach of a world spirit.

canonical_statement: The collective unconscious or universal spirit contains archetypal images that manifest in human perception.

attributions.surface_quote: A vast image out of Spiritus Mundi troubles my sight.

canonical_statement: The material world is the creation of a demiurgic entity known as Ialdabaoth.

attributions.surface_quote: Ialdabaoth, the creator of the material world

canonical_statement: The structure of the universe is organized into seven distinct planetary spheres or levels of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: These seven planets are identical with the Hindu Sapta-lokas

canonical_statement: The material and spiritual realms are hierarchically divided into lower and superior spheres.

attributions.surface_quote: the seven places or spheres, or the superior and inferior worlds

canonical_statement: An esoteric tradition of secret knowledge persists across all ages and cultures.

attributions.surface_quote: The Gnosis, or traditional secret knowledge, was never without its representatives in any age.

canonical_statement: Individual revelation and personal knowledge are efficacious means of accessing truth.

attributions.surface_quote: A belief in the efficacy of individual revelation and individual knowledge.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness possesses the potential to transcend human law and exert influence over divine entities through the acquisition of gnosis.

attributions.surface_quote: man's affinity with the gods... may even subdue the gods by the sheer power of gnosis.

canonical_statement: The ultimate divine principle, Abraxas, exists as a paradoxical unity that transcends binary oppositions such as good and evil, light and dark.

attributions.surface_quote: Abraxas begetteth truth and lying, good and evil... in the same word and act.

canonical_statement: The divine is not an external transcendent entity but is located within the unconscious psyche.

attributions.surface_quote: criticism... had located God in the unconscious.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, or pleroma, manifests itself through the paradoxical nature of Abraxas.

attributions.surface_quote: Had the pleroma a being, Abraxas would be its manifestation.

canonical_statement: The self is a complexio oppositorum, a totality encompassing both conscious and unconscious processes.

attributions.surface_quote: the self... a complexio oppositorum

canonical_statement: Wholeness is achieved through the conscious integration of the unconscious, including the shadow.

attributions.surface_quote: Self-knowledge is achieved through the conscious assimilation of the contents of the unconscious

canonical_statement: Evil is an active, primordial principle rather than a mere absence of good.

attributions.surface_quote: gnostic insistence on evil as an active principle

canonical_statement: The ego is subordinate to a larger, supraordinate psychic authority.

attributions.surface_quote: ego when it can no longer hide... that it has been dethroned by a supraordinate authority

canonical_statement: The psyche functions as an autonomous source of objective knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: the psyche existed as a source of knowledge

canonical_statement: Spiritual transformation requires the integration of both masculine and feminine principles.

attributions.surface_quote: primordial image of the spirit... a feminine principle

canonical_statement: The divine source of existence encompasses and reconciles both benevolent and malevolent polarities.

attributions.surface_quote: God, a God whose name is Abraxas, uniting the godly and devilish elements.

canonical_statement: The perceived distinction between the individual self and the external other is an illusion.

attributions.surface_quote: blurring the distinction between the other and the inner.

canonical_statement: The human psyche is not a singular entity but a multiplicity of potential states and impulses.

attributions.surface_quote: there are not two but a thousand souls clamoring within him.

canonical_statement: Transcendental reality is located exclusively within the interiority of the individual rather than in an external realm.

attributions.surface_quote: Only within yourself exists that other reality.

canonical_statement: The manifest world is devoid of inherent meaning.

attributions.surface_quote: meaning is not to be discovered in the manifest world.

canonical_statement: Meaning is located exclusively within the human psyche.

attributions.surface_quote: By situating meaning within the human psyche

canonical_statement: The world is experienced as an alien environment, generating a desire for escape.

attributions.surface_quote: experience of the world as an alien place . . . a horror of existence

canonical_statement: Human consciousness is the mechanism through which the Godhead achieves self-knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: the Godhead’s evolving self-knowledge through man

canonical_statement: Gnosticism is characterized by the attempt to resolve worldly evil through the promise of a revolutionary new reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Gnosticism as an attempt to solve the ills and evils of this world.

canonical_statement: Anti-cosmic dualism allows for two opposing ethical responses: ascetic withdrawal or total immersion in worldly experience.

attributions.surface_quote: Ascetic withdrawal is one ethical response... An opposite stance is to immerse oneself.

canonical_statement: The material world may be the creation of an inferior deity who mistakenly identifies as the supreme God.

attributions.surface_quote: The work of an inferior deity, a Demiurge, who wrongly believed himself to be God.

canonical_statement: Human existence can be understood as a reenactment of the divine drama of the fallen Wisdom goddess.

attributions.surface_quote: Justine plays out on this earth the drama of the gnostic Wisdom goddess.

canonical_statement: The universe originates from the emotional turbulence and imperfection of a divine emanation.

attributions.surface_quote: the universe is formed out of her agony and remorse.

canonical_statement: Existence is defined by a fundamental dualism between the self and the material world.

attributions.surface_quote: It is a split between self and world, men’s alienation from nature.

canonical_statement: The human condition is characterized by an inherent sense of being cast into a groundless reality.

attributions.surface_quote: the image of having been thrown.

canonical_statement: Liberation is achieved through the cognitive recognition of the circumstances of one's existential origin.

attributions.surface_quote: freedom is the knowledge of wherein we have been thrown.

canonical_statement: Authentic existence and freedom are located exclusively in the immediate present moment between past and future.

attributions.surface_quote: Genuine existence, freedom, dwells only in the crisis between past and future.

canonical_statement: The material universe is an antagonistic or indifferent environment into which human consciousness is cast.

attributions.surface_quote: Gnostic man is thrown into an antagonistic, anti-divine, and therefore anti-human nature.

canonical_statement: Memory and dream are inextricably blended within the structure of the universe.

attributions.surface_quote: Memory and dream are intermixed in this mad universe.

canonical_statement: The material universe is governed by a flawed, ignorant, or deranged creator deity distinct from the true, transcendent God.

attributions.surface_quote: The creator deity, not the true God. That's Yaldabaoth. He's deranged.

canonical_statement: Human consciousness is a fragmented component of a universal Mind that is itself currently in a state of derangement.

attributions.surface_quote: We, as parts of the universe, the Brain, are partly deranged.

canonical_statement: Individual existence on Earth is characterized by alienation from a higher, true origin.

attributions.surface_quote: Sojourn on this planet is a tragic separation from their true home.

canonical_statement: The divine essence is fragmented and distributed across individual human consciousnesses.

attributions.surface_quote: fragments of divinity lose and remember themselves in human minds.

canonical_statement: Gnosticism functions as a system of radical deconstruction that invalidates traditional hierarchies and genealogical structures.

attributions.surface_quote: Gnosticism was the inaugural and most powerful of Deconstructions because it undid all genealogies.

canonical_statement: The relationship between the microcosm and the macrocosm is fundamentally allegorical rather than literal.

attributions.surface_quote: allegorized every microcosm/macrocosm relation.

canonical_statement: Reality is a construct of individual consciousness rather than an objective external substrate.

attributions.surface_quote: Our own mental constructs, he claims, are our knowledge.

canonical_statement: Human beings possess the capacity to define their own existence and universe through self-generated symbols.

attributions.surface_quote: Human beings are becoming gnostic creatures constituting themselves, determining their universe.

canonical_statement: The divine or demiurgic influence is an internal psychological condition that must be overcome within the self.

attributions.surface_quote: It is in ourselves and in ourselves alone that we must attack and destroy Ialdabaoth.

canonical_statement: Existence is characterized by immanence, lacking a shared or transcendent metaphysical substance.

attributions.surface_quote: personal invented mythology and metaphors with no shared metaphysical substance.

canonical_statement: Cultural identity is defined by peripheral conflicts of inclusion and exclusion rather than by stable, central norms.

attributions.surface_quote: cultures define themselves not at their calm centers, but at their peripheral conflicts
